rw: ETL stands for extract, transform and load, the standard way to pull data from sources, clean and reshape it, and place it into a target system.

ww.Edit, test and launch a website in three: Editing, testing and launching a website describes a software release cycle, not ETL, which is about moving and reshaping data between systems rather than publishing web pages.
ww.Enter, track and log expenses for a busi: Entering, tracking and logging expenses is bookkeeping work done by a business, and none of those steps match the extract, transform and load stages that define ETL.
ww.Encrypt, tag and lock files on a compute: Encrypting, tagging and locking files is a security task for protecting storage, while ETL is a data integration process that does not aim to lock anything.

rw: A data warehouse gathers data from many source systems into one central store, organized so analysts can run reports and queries across the whole organization.

ww.A device that cleans data from a compute: A device that wipes a disk is a data eraser or sanitizer, which destroys data, while a data warehouse is built to keep and organize data for analysis.
ww.A program that edits photos and adds fil: Photo editing and filter programs work on images for social media, and they have no role in storing combined business data for reporting, which is what a warehouse does.
ww.A building for storing boxes and pallets: A building holding boxes and pallets is a physical goods warehouse, and the word here is only borrowed, since a data warehouse stores digital records, not shipping stock.

rw: A data pipeline is a series of automated steps that collects data from a source, processes it, and delivers it to a destination such as a warehouse.

ww.A list of all employees and their pay fo: A list of employees and yearly pay is a payroll report, which is a static record of values, not a series of steps that moves data between systems.
ww.A pipe carrying water to the servers in: A water pipe cooling servers is physical plumbing for hardware, and it carries no data, while a data pipeline moves information through software stages.
ww.A chart that shows pipeline pressure in: A chart of pressure in oil and gas lines is an engineering display for physical pipelines, and it has nothing to do with moving data between computer systems.

rw: No-code AI tools offer visual interfaces and prebuilt components so people can build simple AI solutions such as classifiers or chatbots without writing programs themselves.

ww.Run AI without any data of any kind in t: No-code tools do not remove data, since AI systems still need data to learn from, so running AI with no data at all is not what they offer.
ww.Write every line of code by hand, with n: Writing every line by hand with no prebuilt parts is the opposite of no-code, which relies on visual blocks and ready-made components instead of hand-written programs.
ww.Remove the need for any thinking by the: No-code tools reduce programming effort but cannot remove thinking, because users still must define the problem, choose data and judge whether the results make sense.

rw: TensorFlow and PyTorch are Python libraries made for defining, building and training neural networks, which is why they are the usual choices for deep learning work.

ww.A music player app: A music player plays audio files and has no features for defining layers, computing gradients or training a neural network, so it cannot do this job.
ww.A web browser app: A web browser displays pages and runs websites, but it is not a framework for building or training neural networks in Python code.
ww.A word processor app: A word processor is made for writing and formatting documents, and it offers no tools for model layers, training loops or numerical computing with Python.

rw: Machine learning lets computers find patterns in data and use them to make predictions, instead of having programmers write out every rule by hand beforehand.

ww.A way for people to learn about machines: Machine learning is not about people studying machines in classes at a factory, since the learner is the computer system, and the learning comes from data.
ww.A type of computer that has no software: A computer without software or an operating system cannot run anything, so it is not machine learning, which is a method that runs as software on normal systems.
ww.A way to store data on a hard drive for: Storing data on a hard drive is data storage, and while ML uses stored data, saving files for later use does not mean a system learns anything.

rw: Supervised learning trains a model on examples that include the correct answers, called labels, so it can learn to predict the answer for new inputs.

ww.Learning in a classroom with a teacher a: Classroom learning with a teacher and a text is human education, and the word supervised in machine learning refers to labeled examples, not to a person teaching in a room.
ww.Learning by trial and error with rewards: Learning by trial and error with rewards and penalties describes reinforcement learning, a different type, because supervised learning uses examples that already contain the right answers.
ww.Learning from unlabeled data with no lab: Learning from data with no labels is unsupervised learning, so it is the opposite of supervised learning, which depends on labeled examples with known answers.

rw: Unsupervised learning looks for structure such as groups or patterns in data that has no labels, so there are no correct answers given in advance.

ww.Learning with a human grading every step: Having a human grade every step is not what defines unsupervised learning, because the term means the data has no labels, not that a grader checks each step.
ww.Learning from labeled examples and answe: Learning from labeled examples with answers is supervised learning, so it is the opposite of unsupervised learning, where the data has no answers attached.
ww.Learning by earning rewards and penaltie: Learning by earning rewards and penalties is reinforcement learning, which uses feedback from actions, while unsupervised learning has no reward signal and no labeled answers.

rw: Reinforcement learning has an agent try actions and receive rewards or penalties, gradually learning which choices lead to the best total reward over time.

ww.Learning by copying a textbook word for: Copying a textbook word for word is memorizing, not reinforcement learning, which improves behavior through feedback from actions taken in an environment instead of copying text.
ww.Learning by grouping unlabeled data into: Grouping unlabeled data into similar clusters is clustering, a form of unsupervised learning, and it involves no actions or rewards, which reinforcement learning needs.
ww.Learning from a fixed set of labeled exa: Learning from a fixed set of prepared labeled examples is supervised learning, while reinforcement learning has no fixed answer key and learns from the results of actions.

rw: Grouping customers into similar segments with no labels is clustering, which is a task of unsupervised learning, since the groups are discovered from the data itself.

ww.Supervised classification only: Supervised classification needs labeled examples that name the right segment for each customer, but this question says there are no labels, so it cannot be used.
ww.Reinforcement learning methods: Reinforcement learning trains an agent through rewards and penalties from actions, which does not fit grouping customers by similarity when no labels or rewards exist.
ww.Manual spreadsheet sorting by hand: Sorting a spreadsheet by hand is manual work and not a type of machine learning, so it does not count as a learning method at all.

rw: Supervised learning trains on emails already labeled spam or not spam, so the model learns from the right answers and then predicts labels for new emails.

ww.No learning at all: No learning at all would mean a fixed rule or guess, so it cannot predict spam well, whereas a model trained on labeled emails can learn the spam signals.
ww.Unsupervised learning: Unsupervised learning works without labels, so it would ignore the spam tags the question gives, and it is better suited to grouping than to predicting a known label.
ww.Reinforcement learning: Reinforcement learning learns from rewards through actions in an environment, which is not the case for predicting a known label from many already labeled emails.

rw: Clustering groups data points so that points in the same group are more similar to each other than to points in other groups, without needing labels.

ww.Deleting duplicate rows from data: Deleting duplicate rows is data cleaning called deduplication, and it does not group points by similarity, which is what clustering means.
ww.Predicting a single number from data: Predicting a single number from data is regression, a supervised task, while clustering does not predict a value and instead finds groups in the data.
ww.Labeling emails as spam or not spam: Labeling emails as spam or not spam is classification, which needs known labels for training, and clustering does not assign preset labels like these.

rw: A decision tree predicts by following a series of yes or no questions about the input, moving down branches until it reaches a leaf with the answer.

ww.A list of company managers and their dir: An org chart of managers and reports is a company hierarchy diagram, not a model, so it makes no predictions even though it has a tree shape.
ww.A table of numbers only, with no questio: A table of numbers with no questions describes plain data, but a decision tree is a model built from branching questions that lead to a prediction.
ww.A tree that grows in a data center near: A physical tree near a data center cooling system has nothing to do with machine learning, and a decision tree is a model, not a plant.

rw: A random forest builds many decision trees on varied samples of the data and combines their votes, which improves accuracy and reduces overfitting compared with one tree.

ww.A single very deep decision tree that is: A single very deep tree trained once is just one decision tree and often overfits, while a random forest uses many trees together for better results.
ww.A tree-planting program for firms that w: A tree-planting program for carbon offsets is about the environment, and random forest is the name of a machine learning method, not a program that plants trees.
ww.A forest of data servers kept cool in a: A forest of servers kept cool in mountains is not a machine learning model, because random forest is an algorithm that combines decision trees, not a place for hardware.

rw: k-NN predicts by finding the k closest examples to a new point and using their labels or values, such as a majority vote, to decide the answer.

ww.A method for deleting nearby files from: Deleting nearby files from a disk is file management, while k-NN is a prediction method that uses neighbors in the data and removes nothing from a disk.
ww.A method for finding a neighborhood on a: Finding a neighborhood on a city map is navigation, and the word neighbors in k-NN refers to similar data points, not to places on a map.
ww.A method that predicts using only the fa: Using only the farthest examples would give the least similar data points, so it reverses the method, since k-NN relies on the nearest examples to the new point.

rw: Linear regression fits a straight line to data so it can predict a number, such as price from size, by reading the value from the line.

ww.A method that draws a pie chart from a s: A pie chart is a way to display shares of a whole, and linear regression is a prediction method, so drawing pie charts does not describe it.
ww.A method that sorts words alphabetically: Sorting words alphabetically is a basic data task and has nothing to do with predicting numbers, which is the purpose of linear regression.
ww.A method that groups data into clusters: Grouping data into clusters of similar items is clustering, an unsupervised task, while linear regression is supervised and predicts a number rather than forming groups.

rw: Substituting size 3 gives 50 plus 20 times 3, which is 50 plus 60, and that equals 110, the predicted price.

ww.60: A result of 60 comes from computing only 20 times 3 and forgetting the intercept of 50, but the full equation adds both, giving 110 in total.
ww.70: A result of 70 comes from adding 50 and 20, which uses size 1 and ignores that the slope must be multiplied by the size of 3.
ww.170: A result of 170 comes from multiplying 50 plus 20 by 3 as one group, but the multiplication applies only to the size term, so the sum is 110.

rw: Logistic regression outputs a probability between 0 and 1 for a category, which makes it a standard choice for yes or no questions such as spam or churn.

ww.Sorting files by size and date on a comp: Sorting files by size and date is basic file management, and logistic regression is a statistical model for predicting categories, not a tool for ordering files.
ww.Drawing a map of the roads and towns in: Drawing a map of roads and towns is cartography, which has no link to logistic regression, a model that estimates the probability of a category.
ww.Predicting a house price from its size a: Predicting a house price from size and location produces a number, which is a task for linear regression, whereas logistic regression predicts the probability of a category.

rw: A neural network is a model built from connected layers of nodes, loosely inspired by brain neurons, that learns patterns by adjusting the links between them.

ww.A group of people who share ideas about: A group of people sharing ideas online is a social network, and the word network here means a human community, not the layered model used in machine learning.
ww.A network of cables and routers linking: A network of cables and routers is computer networking hardware, which carries data between devices and does not learn patterns the way a neural network does.
ww.A website that stores brain scans for me: A website storing brain scans is a medical data archive, while a neural network is a computing model that only takes loose inspiration from the brain.

rw: Deep learning is machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers, which lets the model learn complex patterns from large amounts of data such as images.

ww.Learning that avoids all computers and u: Learning without computers using books only is ordinary study, whereas deep learning is a machine learning method that runs on computers and uses large amounts of data.
ww.Learning that takes a long time to study: A long degree program is deep study by a person, but deep learning refers to the many layers in a neural network, not to the time spent studying.
ww.Learning with a very small data set of t: Deep learning usually needs large data sets, so a very small set of ten rows or fewer is the opposite of how it is normally used.

rw: Weights are numbers on the connections between nodes that set how strongly each input affects a node, and training adjusts them to improve predictions.

ww.The speed of the internet link between s: The speed of a network link between servers is bandwidth, which is a hardware measure and has no role in how a neural network handles its inputs.
ww.The size of the data file saved on the c: The size of a data file on disk is a storage measure, while weights are learned numbers inside the model that scale the inputs.
ww.The physical weight of the computer in k: The physical weight of a computer in kilograms is a hardware fact, and the weights of a neural network are mathematical values, not a measure of mass.

rw: Gradient descent changes model parameters in small steps in the direction that lowers the error, repeating until the loss is as small as it can get.

ww.Raises the error on purpose at every ste: Raising the error on purpose would make the model worse, while gradient descent takes steps that lower the error, so this reverses its aim.
ww.Deletes the training data after every ro: Deleting training data after every round would leave nothing to learn from, and gradient descent keeps the data while it updates the model values.
ww.Sorts features alphabetically so columns: Sorting features alphabetically is a layout choice that changes nothing about the model error, so it is not what gradient descent does during training.

rw: A loss function measures how wrong a model's predictions are compared with the true values, giving training a number it tries to make smaller.

ww.A tool that deletes data from a table or: A tool that deletes data is a data removal command, but a loss function is a number that measures prediction error and does not alter any table or file.
ww.A count of how many features exist in th: Counting the features in a data set gives its width, which is a description of the data, while a loss function scores the quality of predictions.
ww.A measure of how fast a model runs and h: How fast a model runs and how much memory it uses are performance costs, but a loss function measures prediction error, not speed or memory.

rw: A hyperparameter is a setting chosen before training starts, such as the learning rate or number of layers, and the model does not learn it from data.

ww.A column of the data set that holds the: A column holding the target values is the label or target column of the data, which the model predicts, and it is not a setting chosen by the builder.
ww.A chart label that names the axes of a g: A chart label naming axes is part of a graph in a report, and has no connection to the settings that control how a model trains.
ww.A value the model learns during training: A value the model learns from the data during training is a parameter such as a weight, while a hyperparameter is set by the builder beforehand.

rw: The learning rate sets how large a step the model takes when it updates its parameters, so a high rate moves fast and a low rate moves slowly.

ww.How often data is backed up to a server: How often data is backed up to the cloud is a backup schedule, which is an operations choice and has no link to how a model updates itself.
ww.How many rows are in the data set used t: The number of rows in a data set is its size, and the learning rate does not count rows and instead controls the size of each update step.
ww.How fast a person learns a new tool when: How fast a person learns a tool is human skill, but in machine learning the learning rate is a training setting that controls the size of update steps.

rw: Cross-validation splits the data into several parts, trains on some and tests on the rest, repeating so every part is tested, which gives a reliable estimate of performance.

ww.Checking a model only once on the data i: Checking a model only once on the data it learned from tells little about new data and hides overfitting, while cross-validation tests on data held out of training.
ww.Validating a user's password twice at lo: Validating a password twice at login is a security step for sign in, and it has nothing to do with checking how well a model performs.
ww.Comparing two different programming lang: Comparing two programming languages is a software choice, and cross-validation is a way to estimate model performance, not a way to compare languages.

rw: Data leakage happens when information from the test set accidentally influences training, which makes the performance look better than it will be on truly new data.

ww.Data being stolen by hackers from a comp: Data stolen by hackers is a security breach, which is a different issue, since data leakage in machine learning is a modeling mistake that makes results look too good.
ww.Data being stored in two places, so a co: Data stored in two places is duplication or redundancy, and it does not describe the modeling error where test information flows into training.
ww.Data being deleted by mistake from a tab: Data deleted by mistake is data loss, which removes information, while data leakage is the opposite problem of unwanted information reaching the training process.

rw: Bias in a model is systematic error that leads to unfair or skewed results, often caused by unbalanced or unrepresentative training data.

ww.A model's favorite color in a chart or a: A favorite color in a chart is a design choice and has nothing to do with the bias that affects model results.
ww.A model's file size on a disk or in a cl: A model's file size is a storage measure, and bias concerns whether predictions are systematically unfair or skewed, not how large the file is.
ww.A model's speed of training, which depen: Training speed depends on data size and hardware, which is a performance matter, while bias is about skewed or unfair predictions and not about speed.

rw: A model trained on past data that favored men learns that pattern, so bias in the training data is the most likely cause of ranking women lower.

ww.Too little electricity: Too little electricity might stop a computer from running, but it cannot make a model favor men over women in its rankings, so it is not the cause.
ww.A broken keyboard cable: A broken keyboard cable affects typing input and has no way to shape how a trained model ranks men and women, so it is unrelated.
ww.Too many colors in the charts: Too many colors in charts affects how reports look, and it cannot change the ranking decisions of a model, which come from the patterns in training data.

rw: Feature engineering means creating or choosing input variables, such as turning a date into day of week, so that they help the model learn useful patterns.

ww.Building a physical machine that sorts a: Building a physical machine that sorts items is mechanical engineering, while feature engineering works on the input variables used to train a model.
ww.Deleting all inputs from a model and sta: Deleting all inputs and restarting would leave the model with no information, whereas feature engineering improves the inputs it already has or builds new ones.
ww.Writing documentation for the model and: Writing documentation is useful for a project, but it does not change the inputs given to a model, so it is not feature engineering.

rw: Dimensionality reduction cuts the number of features while keeping the important information, which makes data simpler to handle and often speeds up training.

ww.Reducing the number of rows to zero in a: Reducing the number of rows to zero would leave no data at all, and dimensionality reduction works on the features, which are the columns, not the rows.
ww.Making charts two-dimensional only and n: Making charts two-dimensional is a display choice, whereas dimensionality reduction changes the number of features in the data used by a model.
ww.Making a data set smaller on the disk by: Compressing files makes them smaller on disk but keeps every feature, while dimensionality reduction cuts the number of features used in the analysis.

rw: The training set is the portion of data used to teach the model, since the model adjusts its parameters by learning patterns from these examples.

ww.A set of machines in a gym used for trai: A set of machines in a gym is exercise equipment, and the training set in machine learning is data, not a group of physical machines.
ww.The portion used to check final performa: The portion used to check final performance is the test set, which is held back, and the training set is the part used to teach the model.
ww.A set of instructions for users of a new: A set of instructions for users of a course is teaching material for people, while a training set is a part of the data given to the model.

rw: A validation set is used to tune a model and choose settings such as hyperparameters during development, without touching the test set that is saved for the end.

ww.Printing the final report of the study f: Printing a final report for managers is communication of results, and it is not the purpose of a validation set, which is used while building the model.
ww.Storing backups of the data on a server: Storing backups in another city is data protection, which has no connection to validation, since a validation set is a part of data used to compare model settings.
ww.Teaching the model first with the labele: Teaching the model first with labeled examples is the job of the training set, whereas the validation set is used afterward to tune and compare settings.

rw: Keeping the test set separate until the end gives an honest estimate of how the model will perform on new data it has never seen.

ww.So the model can learn from it faster, a: Letting the model learn from the test set would contaminate it, and a model that trains on test data gives scores that look better than they really are.
ww.So it uses less memory on the computer d: Memory use is not the reason, since the test set is kept apart to avoid bias in the score, not to save memory during the training run.
ww.So no one can see the data until the ver: The point is not secrecy from people, since the test set is kept unused in training so the final score is a fair measure, not hidden from viewers.

rw: Transfer learning reuses a model trained on one task as a starting point for another task, which saves time and data compared with training from nothing.

ww.Transferring money between accounts at a: Moving money between bank accounts is a financial transaction, and transfer learning in AI is about reusing a trained model, not about funds.
ww.Copying a file to a USB drive to carry i: Copying a file to a USB drive only moves data from one place to another, and it does not reuse learned knowledge as transfer learning does.
ww.Moving a model to another computer so it: Moving a model to a faster computer is deployment or hardware migration, but transfer learning reuses what a model already learned for a new task, not where it runs.

rw: Model deployment means putting a trained model into use, for example in an app or service, so that people or other systems can get its predictions.

ww.Writing the model's documentation and a: Writing documentation and a guide helps users understand a model, but it does not put the model into use, which is what deployment means.
ww.Training a model on more data to raise i: Training on more data to raise accuracy is part of model development, which happens before deployment, since deployment is about using the trained model in practice.
ww.Deleting a model after training to free: Deleting a model after training would remove it from use, whereas deployment makes a trained model available so it can serve real users or systems.

rw: Real-world data can change over time, so a deployed model's predictions may become less accurate, and monitoring detects this early so the model can be updated.

ww.Models never change after deployment, so: Models can degrade after deployment because the world changes, so the claim that they never change and need no checks is false, and monitoring is needed.
ww.Monitoring is required only by law and n: Monitoring is not only a legal duty, because teams also do it to catch falling accuracy, drift and errors, and these practical reasons matter regardless of law.
ww.Models improve automatically without dat: Models do not improve by themselves without new data or updates, since a deployed model stays fixed unless people retrain it, which is why monitoring matters.

rw: Concept drift is a change over time in the relationship between inputs and outcomes, so a model that once predicted well may become less accurate.

ww.A slow internet connection that delays p: A slow internet connection delays page loading, which is a network issue and has no link to how a model's input and output relationship changes.
ww.A change in office layout when desks are: A change in office layout is about workspace and furniture, whereas concept drift is a change in the pattern a model has learned from data.
ww.A flickering computer screen caused by a: A flickering screen from a loose cable is a hardware fault, and concept drift describes a shift in the data pattern, not a display problem.

rw: Overfitting is when a model learns the training data too closely, including noise, and then does poorly on new data it has not seen.

ww.A model that uses too little storage spa: Using too little storage space is a resource matter, but overfitting concerns how a model learns, so file storage on a disk does not define it.
ww.A model that is too simple to learn the: A model too simple to learn the patterns in the data is underfitting, which is the opposite problem to overfitting, where the model is too closely fitted.
ww.A model that runs too fast and so cannot: Running fast does not make a model overfit or untrustworthy, since overfitting is about poor performance on new data after memorizing the training set.

rw: More training data gives the model more variety, and a simpler model has less room to memorize noise, so both steps help reduce overfitting.

ww.Training for much longer on the same dat: Training much longer on the same data lets the model memorize it even more, so it tends to increase overfitting and not reduce it.
ww.Adding many irrelevant features to the d: Adding many irrelevant features gives the model more noise to memorize, which raises the risk of overfitting instead of lowering it.
ww.Using only a few training examples for t: Using only a few training examples makes it easier for a model to memorize them, so this tends to worsen overfitting.

rw: An ensemble method combines several models, for example by voting or averaging, so the group gives a better prediction than most single models alone would.

ww.Splitting data into a single column to s: Splitting data into a single column to save space changes how data is stored, and it has no link to combining models, which is what an ensemble does.
ww.Using a single very large model trained: A single very large model trained once is not an ensemble, because an ensemble uses several models whose outputs are combined for a better result.
ww.Playing music during training to keep th: Playing music during training has no effect on a model, and an ensemble method is about combining models and not about the mood of the staff.

rw: Collaborative filtering suggests items that users with similar tastes liked, using patterns in ratings or behavior across many users to predict what someone will enjoy.

ww.One that filters spam from emails and bl: Filtering spam from emails is a classification task for security, and it has nothing to do with suggesting items based on what similar users liked.
ww.One that suggests random items only, cho: A system that suggests random items by chance gives no personal value, whereas collaborative filtering uses the behavior of other users to choose its suggestions.
ww.One that suggests items by price only, l: Suggesting items by price only is simple sorting that ignores user tastes, while collaborative filtering relies on the preferences of similar users.

rw: Suggesting a show because people with similar watch histories enjoyed it is collaborative filtering, which recommends items using the preferences of similar users.

ww.Speech recognition AI: Speech recognition AI turns spoken words into text, which is a different task from suggesting a show based on what similar viewers watched.
ww.Data encryption tools: Data encryption tools protect information by scrambling it, which is a security task and does not produce show suggestions for viewers.
ww.Rule-based programming: Rule-based programming follows fixed rules written by people, while this suggestion comes from patterns found across many viewers, which is collaborative filtering.

rw: Perception in AI is a system's ability to interpret sensory input such as images or sound, which lets it make sense of what is around it.

ww.A system's ability to print documents an: Printing documents and sending them to a printer is an output task, while perception is about understanding input from the world.
ww.A system's ability to rewrite its own ha: Rewriting its own hardware to run faster is not how AI systems work and has nothing to do with perception, which is interpreting sensory input.
ww.A system's ability to store large files: Storing large files on internal disk drives is a storage function, whereas perception is the ability to interpret sensory input such as images or sound.

rw: Object detection finds objects inside an image and labels them, usually marking each one with a box, such as a car or a person.

ww.Counting pages in a book or a long repor: Counting pages in a book is a simple counting task on documents, and object detection works on images to find and label things in them.
ww.Finding spelling mistakes in a typed doc: Finding spelling mistakes is a text checking task, while object detection looks at pictures, not typed documents, to find items.
ww.Detecting power failures in an electric: Detecting power failures in a grid is an engineering monitoring task, and object detection is a computer vision task that finds objects in images.

rw: Image classification assigns one label to a whole image, such as cat or dog, based on what the picture mostly shows.

ww.Printing an image on paper with a color: Printing an image on paper is an output task for a printer, and image classification is an AI task that assigns a label to a picture.
ww.Making an image larger by zooming in on: Zooming in on a screen only changes how large an image looks, and it does not assign a label to the picture, which classification does.
ww.Drawing a box around every object in an: Drawing a box around every object with a label is object detection, while image classification gives one label to the whole image without locating objects.

rw: OCR converts text in images, such as scanned pages or photos of signs, into editable text that a computer can search and change.

ww.Converting video into photos, frame by f: Converting video into photos frame by frame is video processing, and OCR reads text found in images instead of splitting video into pictures.
ww.Converting speech into written text file: Converting speech into written text is speech recognition, which works on audio, while OCR works on images that contain printed or written text.
ww.Converting text into spoken audio files: Converting text into spoken audio is speech synthesis, which goes in the opposite direction from OCR, which reads text from an image.

rw: Knowledge representation organizes information in a form that a computer can use to reason, such as facts, rules or graphs, so it can draw conclusions.

ww.Deleting information that the computer c: Deleting information that cannot be stored easily would lose knowledge, whereas knowledge representation structures information so that a computer can use it.
ww.Showing information on a large screen to: Showing information on a large screen is a display task, and it does not organize facts into a form a computer can reason with.
ww.Storing information in a notebook kept o: Storing information in a notebook on a shelf keeps it on paper, where a computer cannot use it, so it is not knowledge representation.

rw: A knowledge graph is a network of connected facts about things and their relationships, with nodes for entities and links showing how they relate.

ww.A chart of student grades in a school fo: A chart of student grades summarizes school results and is not a network of facts, which is what a knowledge graph is.
ww.A graph of a company's profits over the: A graph of company profits is a business chart showing numbers over time, while a knowledge graph links entities and their relationships.
ww.A list of definitions in alphabetical or: A list of definitions in alphabetical order is a glossary or dictionary, and it does not link facts to each other the way a knowledge graph does.

rw: Logical reasoning in AI draws conclusions from known facts and rules, so if the facts are true and the rules are valid, the result follows.

ww.Copying text from the web into a documen: Copying text from the web into a document is data entry and does not involve drawing conclusions, which is what logical reasoning means.
ww.Guessing without any facts at all or pro: Guessing without facts or proof is the opposite of logical reasoning, which depends on facts and rules to reach valid conclusions.
ww.Storing data in a list on a computer dis: Storing data in a list on a disk is storage and does not draw conclusions from facts and rules, which defines logical reasoning.

rw: The invoice is $1,500, which is over $1,000, so the rule applies and the reasoning system concludes that it needs approval.

ww.It must be deleted: Deleting the invoice is not supported by the rule, which only says invoices over $1,000 need approval, so nothing in it calls for deletion.
ww.It must be paid now: The rule says nothing about paying the invoice now, and it only requires approval first, so a reasoning system cannot conclude it must be paid.
ww.It needs no approval: Since 1,500 is greater than 1,000, the rule applies, so saying it needs no approval contradicts the rule and the system would not reach that conclusion.

rw: An embedding is a list of numbers, a vector, that represents the meaning of data such as a word, so similar items get similar vectors.

ww.A password stored in code and hidden fro: A password hidden in code is a secret credential, which is a security matter and not a numeric representation of meaning, as an embedding is.
ww.A video placed on a website to explain a: A video placed on a website to explain a product is media content, and the word embedding here means a vector, not a page element.
ww.A photo added inside a document by a use: A photo added inside a document is an embedded image in the everyday sense, but an embedding in AI is a vector of numbers for meaning.

rw: Embeddings place similar items close together as vectors, so models can measure how similar items are, which helps in search, recommendations and clustering.

ww.They permanently remove all errors from: Embeddings do not remove errors from text, since they are numeric representations of meaning, and nothing about them permanently corrects mistakes in the words.
ww.They make data impossible to read for th: Embeddings are made for models to use, and they do not hide data from the user, so making data unreadable is not their purpose.
ww.They replace the need for training a mod: Models still need training to use embeddings well, so embeddings help the work but they do not replace training a model.

rw: A search algorithm in AI explores possible options step by step, such as paths or moves, to find a solution to a problem.

ww.A way of hiding a website from search en: Hiding a website from search engines is a web publishing setting, and a search algorithm in AI explores options to find a solution.
ww.A program that prints search results on: Printing search results on paper is an output task for a printer, and it does not explore options the way an AI search algorithm does.
ww.A tool for deleting search history from: Deleting search history is a privacy action in a browser, while an AI search algorithm explores options to solve a problem.

rw: A navigation app searches over the possible paths between two cities and picks the best one, such as the shortest, which is the search idea in AI.

ww.Generating new roads on the map to short: Generating new roads would change the map, but a navigation app does not build roads, and it only looks for the best route over roads that exist.
ww.Converting speech into text for the driv: Converting speech into text is speech recognition, which may help with voice commands, but it is not how the app finds the shortest route.
ww.Compressing the map image to save room o: Compressing the map image saves storage, which is a file task, and it does not help the app find the shortest route between two cities.

rw: Sentiment analysis uses AI to decide whether text expresses positive, negative or neutral feelings, which is useful for reviews, posts and customer messages.

ww.Translating text from one language to an: Translating text between languages is machine translation, which changes the language of the text and does not measure whether the feelings expressed are positive or negative.
ww.Checking text for spelling mistakes and: Checking spelling and grammar is proofreading, which fixes writing errors and does not decide whether the text shows positive or negative feelings.
ww.Counting the words in a document and the: Counting words and pages is simple document statistics, which measures size, and does not tell whether the writer feels positive or negative.

rw: A negative sentiment score suggests that the reviews express negative feelings, so customers are unhappy with the product or service.

ww.The reviews are too short to be read by: Reviews being too short would cause missing or weak results, but a negative score says something about the feeling in the text, not about its length.
ww.Customers are very happy with the produc: Customers who are very happy would give positive text and a positive score, so a negative score suggests the opposite of this.
ww.The reviews were in French so the softwa: A failure on French text would show up as an error or missing result, while a negative score is a valid result showing negative feelings.

rw: Speech synthesis creates spoken audio from text, often called text to speech, and it is used in voice assistants and screen readers.

ww.Removing noise from audio files: Removing noise from audio files is audio cleaning or noise reduction, which improves a recording and does not create speech from written text.
ww.Recognizing spoken words as text: Recognizing spoken words as text is speech recognition, which is the reverse of speech synthesis, since synthesis starts from text and produces audio.
ww.Recording a live conversation call: Recording a live conversation call captures sound that already exists, whereas speech synthesis generates new spoken audio from written text with a computer.

rw: A sensor is a device that collects information from the environment, such as a camera, microphone or radar, and passes it to the AI system.

ww.A program that edits videos by adding ti: A program that edits videos is software for media editing, and it does not collect information from the environment, which is the role of a sensor.
ww.A screen that shows results of the work: A screen that shows results is an output device, while a sensor is an input device that gathers information about the surroundings.
ww.A tool that stores data from the system: A tool that stores data for later use is a storage device, and a sensor instead gathers new information from the environment.

rw: Using cameras and radar to sense the surroundings is perception, the stage in which an AI system gathers and interprets data about its environment.

ww.Writing its own manual first: Writing its own manual does not describe cameras and radar, which are sensing tools used to understand the road and not to produce documents.
ww.Storing old files on a disk: Storing old files on a disk is a data storage task, and it does not describe how cameras and radar are used to sense the road.
ww.Reporting its profits to owners: Reporting profits to owners is a business reporting task and has no link to the cameras and radar that a self-driving car uses to sense its surroundings.

rw: Planning in AI means choosing a sequence of actions to reach a goal, such as a robot working out the steps to move an object.

ww.Scheduling employee holidays for the yea: Scheduling employee holidays is a human resources job, and although it is called planning in daily speech, AI planning means choosing actions to reach a goal.
ww.Printing a plan on paper for the whole t: Printing a plan on paper is a document task that outputs a file, whereas AI planning is the process of working out which actions to take.
ww.Writing a company's yearly budget with f: Writing a yearly budget is a finance task, and AI planning is about picking actions that reach a goal, not about preparing budgets.

rw: Uncertainty means not being sure of facts or outcomes, and AI systems often handle it with probability, for example by giving a likelihood instead of a sure answer.

ww.A guarantee that all answers are right,: Uncertainty is the opposite of a guarantee that all answers are right, since strict logic cannot promise this when facts are missing or unclear.
ww.A feeling that machines have when they a: Machines do not have feelings of dread before a crash, so uncertainty in AI is about incomplete knowledge and not an emotion.
ww.A rule that blocks all decisions made by: Uncertainty is not a rule that blocks manager decisions, because it describes how sure a system is about facts, and systems still make decisions under it.

rw: Data privacy means protecting personal information from being misused or seen by the wrong people, and giving individuals some control over how their data is used.

ww.Publishing every customer's details onli: Publishing every customer's details online would expose personal information, which is the opposite of data privacy, since privacy protects such details from being seen.
ww.Making data as large as possible so that: Making data as large as possible has no link to privacy, which is about who can access personal information and how it is used, not about size.
ww.Keeping data in a locked room only and n: Keeping data in a locked room and never using computers is not what privacy means, since privacy is about protecting information while still allowing safe and proper use.

rw: PII is information that can identify a specific person, such as a name, address, phone number or national ID, alone or when combined with other data.

ww.Information that is true for everyone in: Information true for everyone in a group is general knowledge and does not point to one person, while PII is data that can identify a specific person.
ww.Information that is always encrypted by: Information being encrypted by default is a protection feature, and it does not define PII, which is data that could identify a person whether or not it is encrypted.
ww.Information that is deleted after use by: Information deleted after use is about retention, which is a different matter, and data can be PII whether or not a firm deletes it.

rw: A home address and phone number can identify a specific person and reach them, so this is PII that needs protection.

ww.The weather forecast for today in your t: The weather forecast for a town is public information about a place and does not identify any person, so it is not PII.
ww.The number of days in a week or a month: The number of days in a week or a month is a general fact and says nothing about any person, so it is not PII.
ww.The average price of milk in a store: The average price of milk is a statistic about a product that does not point to a person, so it does not count as PII.

rw: Anonymization removes or hides details that identify individuals, such as names and ID numbers, so the data can be used with a lower privacy risk.

ww.Adding a person's name to every record t: Adding names to every record would make people easier to identify, which is the opposite of anonymization, which aims to hide identities.
ww.Making data larger by adding more rows t: Adding more rows increases data volume and does not protect identities, so it is not anonymization, which is about hiding who the records describe.
ww.Copying data to a public site for anyone: Copying data to a public site makes it available to anyone, which puts privacy at risk and does not anonymize anything.

rw: Combining details such as birth date, zip code and gender can single someone out, because few people share the same combination, so anonymized data can still be linked to a person.

ww.Computers can read minds and so they can: Computers cannot read minds, and re-identification happens when data already holds details that can be matched, not because machines know things from nothing.
ww.Anonymous data always contains names, so: Truly anonymous data has names removed, so saying it always contains names is false, and the real risk comes from other details that can be combined.
ww.Anonymous data is never stored anywhere,: Anonymous data is stored somewhere like any data set, so claiming it is never stored is false, and traceability comes from combining details.

rw: Informed consent means people understand how their data will be collected and used and then agree to it, which keeps data collection fair and open.

ww.People are required to share all data wi: Informed consent is voluntary, so a requirement to share all data with any firm that asks contradicts it, since people must be free to agree or refuse.
ww.Data is collected without telling anyone: Collecting data without telling anyone and using it for any purpose breaks informed consent, which requires that people know and agree beforehand.
ww.People are tricked into sharing data the: Tricking people into sharing private data removes real consent, since informed consent depends on honest information and a free choice.

rw: Data minimization means collecting only the data you actually need for a stated purpose, which lowers privacy risk and the harm if a breach occurs.

ww.Delete data after first use and keep no: Deleting data after first use with no copy is an extreme retention rule, but data minimization means collecting only what is needed, not erasing at once.
ww.Collect as much data as possible each da: Collecting as much data as possible each day is the opposite of data minimization, which limits collection to what a purpose actually requires.
ww.Share data with every partner firm we kn: Sharing data with every partner firm increases exposure of personal information, and data minimization aims to limit data use, not spread it widely.

rw: A data breach is an incident in which private data is accessed or exposed without permission, whether by an attack, a mistake or a lost device.

ww.A report about data quality that is sent: A data quality report sent to managers is a routine management document and does not describe an incident where data is exposed.
ww.A planned backup of the data that is run: A planned nightly backup is a protective routine and is done with permission, so it is not a breach, which is unauthorized access to data.
ww.A chart that shows sales by region and b: A chart of sales by region and month is a business report that shows results and does not describe an incident of unauthorized access.

rw: The right first step is to contain the breach to stop further loss and notify affected people as required, so they can protect themselves.

ww.Blame the customers for the attack and d: Blaming customers and delaying contact is wrong and unethical, because customers did not cause the attack and they need prompt notice to protect themselves.
ww.Hide the problem from customers so as no: Hiding the problem from customers breaks trust and often the law, since many rules require prompt notice, so concealment makes the harm worse.
ww.Delete the evidence of the attack and ca: Deleting evidence of the attack destroys what investigators need and may be illegal, and carrying on as usual leaves the weakness open to attackers.

rw: Encryption scrambles data using a key so only authorized people with the key can read it, which protects it if it is stolen or intercepted.

ww.Deleting data permanently from all of th: Deleting data permanently from servers is erasure, which removes the data, whereas encryption keeps the data and scrambles it so only authorized people can read it.
ww.Copying data to another drive for use as: Copying data to another drive is a backup, which keeps another copy of the data and does not scramble it or limit who can read it.
ww.Making data easier for all to read by re: Removing passwords makes data easier for anyone to read, which weakens protection, while encryption does the opposite by making data unreadable without the key.

rw: Multi-factor authentication requires two or more ways to prove identity, such as a password plus a code, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

ww.Writing a password on a note and stickin: Writing a password on a note on a screen exposes it to anyone who sees it, which is poor security and not a second factor.
ww.Sharing a password with a team to make a: Sharing a password with a team weakens security and gives one factor to many people, while multi-factor authentication adds independent proofs of identity for one person.
ww.Using one very long password only, chang: A single long password is still only one factor, so even changed yearly it does not meet the two or more proofs that multi-factor authentication needs.

rw: GDPR is the European Union law that protects the personal data and privacy of people in the EU, and it gives them rights over their data.

ww.Trade secrets of European firms under un: GDPR protects personal data of individuals and not the trade secrets of firms, which are covered by other business laws, so this option misstates its scope.
ww.The speed of the European internet netwo: GDPR is a data protection law and does not regulate how fast European networks run, so the speed of the internet is outside its scope.
ww.The prices of goods in Europe and their: Goods prices and taxes are matters of trade and tax law, and GDPR deals with personal data, so it does not set prices.

rw: CCPA gives California residents the right to know what personal data is collected, to delete it, and to opt out of its sale.

ww.A right to see anyone's data held by any: CCPA covers personal data held by businesses that meet its rules, so it does not let residents see anyone's data from any company in any country.
ww.A right to free internet access at home: CCPA is a privacy law and does not provide internet service, so free access at home from any provider is not one of its rights.
ww.A right to avoid all taxes on goods and: CCPA does not exempt anyone from taxes on online sales, since it is about personal data privacy and has no effect on tax duties.

rw: COPPA, the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act, protects the online privacy of children under 13 by requiring parental consent before sites collect their personal data.

ww.Prices of online goods and services: Prices of online goods are a consumer and trade matter, while COPPA is a law about the privacy of children online, so it does not cover prices.
ww.Online privacy of adults over 65: COPPA protects children, not adults over 65, so this option names the wrong group, because the law centers on the online privacy of young children.
ww.Copyrights on music and film works: Copyrights on music and film are covered by copyright law, and COPPA is a privacy law, so the similar sounding name does not mean it covers copyright.

rw: HIPAA protects the privacy and security of health information, such as medical records held by providers and insurers, and sets rules on who may see them.

ww.The privacy of voter choices in an elect: Voter choices are protected by election laws and the secret ballot, and HIPAA is a law about health information, so it does not cover voting.
ww.The privacy of bank accounts and the rec: Bank accounts and financial records are covered by financial privacy laws, whereas HIPAA covers health information, so this option names the wrong subject.
ww.The privacy of school grades and test sc: School grades and test scores fall under education privacy law, FERPA, and HIPAA covers health information, so this option mixes up the two laws.

rw: FERPA, the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, protects the privacy of student education records, such as grades, and gives students and parents rights over them.

ww.The privacy of bank records and accounts: Bank records and accounts are covered by financial privacy rules, not FERPA, which is an education privacy law, so this option names the wrong area.
ww.The privacy of medical records at hospit: Medical records at hospitals are protected by health privacy law, HIPAA, and FERPA covers education records, so this option confuses the two laws.
ww.The privacy of phone calls and texts: Phone calls and texts are covered by communications and wiretap laws, which differ from FERPA, a law that deals with student education records.

rw: AI ethics is the set of principles about developing and using AI in fair, safe and responsible ways, so that it benefits people and avoids harm.

ww.Rules for buying AI hardware such as chi: Rules for buying AI hardware are purchasing policy, and AI ethics deals with how AI is built and used and its effects on people.
ww.A method for storing AI models on a serv: Storing AI models in a secure data center is a security and operations task, and it does not address fairness, safety or responsibility, which define ethics.
ww.Rules that make AI run faster on a compu: Making AI run faster with better chips is a performance goal, whereas AI ethics is about whether AI is used fairly, safely and responsibly.

rw: Algorithmic bias is when an algorithm produces unfair outcomes that favor or harm certain groups, often because of skewed training data or flawed design choices.

ww.An algorithm that writes poetry and song: An algorithm writing poetry describes a creative use of AI, and it does not describe unfair outcomes for groups, which is what algorithmic bias means.
ww.An algorithm that runs quickly and so gi: Running quickly does not cause bias, because bias comes from skewed data or design choices, and speed alone does not make results differ across groups.
ww.An algorithm with no input data and so n: An algorithm with no input data could not produce results at all, so it cannot be biased, and this option describes a broken system and not bias.

rw: Approving fewer applicants from one neighborhood when finances are equal shows an unfair pattern against a group, which is algorithmic bias, often from skewed data.

ww.Better accuracy: Better accuracy would mean the model predicts well for everyone, but approving fewer applicants from one neighborhood with equal finances points to unfair treatment, so accuracy is not the issue.
ww.Faster processing: Faster processing concerns speed, and it would not explain why equally qualified applicants from one neighborhood are approved less often, which is an issue of fairness.
ww.Data compression: Data compression reduces file size and has no effect on who is approved, so it cannot explain unequal approval for equal finances.

rw: Using diverse, representative data and testing results across groups helps find and fix unfair patterns, which is the best way to reduce bias.

ww.Training on data from one group only, so: Training on one group only makes the system learn well for that group and poorly for others, so it increases bias and does not reduce it.
ww.Never testing the model on any group of: Never testing the model on any group before release would leave bias unnoticed, so it fails to reduce bias and risks harm to people.
ww.Removing human review entirely, so that: Removing human review entirely lets biased decisions pass unchecked, whereas people can catch unfair results, so this step would raise bias.

rw: Transparency means being open about how a system works and makes decisions, so users and regulators can understand, question and check its results.

ww.Hiding how a system works from users and: Hiding how a system works from users and regulators is the opposite of transparency, which depends on openness about how the system makes decisions.
ww.Making the screen see-through so users c: Making a screen see-through is a literal reading of the word, but transparency in AI is about being open on how the system works.
ww.Using only small data sets that fit in o: Using only small data sets has no link to openness about how decisions are made, which is what transparency in AI is about.

rw: Explainable AI means the decisions of the system can be understood by people, with clear reasons given for why it produced a result.

ww.AI that refuses to answer questions so i: An AI that refuses to answer questions is not explainable, and avoiding answers does not make its decisions understandable, so this does not match the idea.
ww.AI that explains jokes and puzzles to it: An AI that explains jokes and puzzles describes a task it performs, but explainable AI is about making the AI's own decisions understandable.
ww.AI that is hidden from users and from au: An AI hidden from users and auditors is the opposite of explainable, because explainability means people can see and understand how decisions are made.

rw: Accountability in AI means there is clear responsibility for the outcomes an AI system causes, so someone answers for its results and for fixing harm.

ww.Counting the money spent on AI projects: Counting the money spent on AI projects is financial accounting, which tracks costs, and it does not assign responsibility for what an AI system does.
ww.Blaming the computer for every error tha: Blaming the computer for every error avoids human responsibility, whereas accountability requires that people or organizations answer for the system.
ww.Hiding who built the system from the pub: Hiding who built the system defeats accountability, since people need to know who is responsible for the outcomes in order to hold them to account.

rw: The organization that deployed the tool chose to use it and benefits from it, so it is accountable for wrong outcomes such as a wrongly denied claim.

ww.Only the software itself and its code: Software cannot be held responsible, because it has no legal duty or ability to make amends, so blaming only the code leaves no accountable party.
ww.The customer who made the claim to the f: The customer only made a claim and did not build or run the tool, so blaming the customer for a wrong denial shifts responsibility to the wrong party.
ww.No one, as the work was fully automated: Automation does not remove responsibility, because people and organizations choose and run these tools, so saying no one is accountable fails customers who are harmed.

rw: A deepfake is fake media created by AI, often a video or audio clip, that makes someone appear to say or do something they never did.

ww.A fast video format that loads in a brow: A fast video format is a technical file type for streaming, and deepfake refers to fake media made by AI, not to loading speed.
ww.A very deep database that stores records: A deep database with nested folders is a storage structure, and the deep in deepfake comes from deep learning, not from levels of folders.
ww.A real video with captions added to show: A real video with captions is genuine footage with text added, while a deepfake is synthetic media that shows something that never happened.

rw: Deepfakes can deceive people and damage reputations, since realistic fake video or audio can spread false claims about a person and erode trust in real media.

ww.They are impossible to create with any s: Deepfakes can be created with many readily available tools, so saying they are impossible to make is false, and that ease is part of the concern.
ww.They cannot be shared online by any user: Deepfakes can be shared online like other media, so saying nobody can share them is false, and wide sharing is why they can cause harm.
ww.They always improve public safety by war: Deepfakes do not always improve safety, and warning people is not their usual use, since they are more often used to mislead, scam or harass.

rw: The copyright concern is whether creators' work was used without permission to train AI, since models may learn from books, art or code that creators own.

ww.Whether the data is too clean to use in: Data being too clean is not a copyright question, as copyright asks whether the data was used with permission, not how tidy it is.
ww.Whether the model is named correctly by: Whether the model is named correctly is a matter of branding and labels, and copyright concerns are about the use of creators' work.
ww.Whether the computer running the model i: The size of the computer running the model is a hardware matter and has no link to whether the training data was used with permission.

rw: Checking permissions and giving proper credit where required respects the rights of creators, and keeps the use of AI content legal and fair.

ww.Selling others' work without asking for: Selling others' work without consent violates their rights and disrespects creators, so it is the opposite of a practice that respects them.
ww.Removing the creator's name from the wor: Removing the creator's name before sharing hides who made the work and denies credit, which disrespects creators and can break the terms of use.
ww.Copying any work found online and passin: Copying work found online and passing it off as your own is plagiarism, which steals credit and breaks copyright, so it fails to respect creators.

rw: Human oversight means people review AI decisions and can override them, so a person keeps control and can correct mistakes before harm results.

ww.Turning off all computers in the office: Turning off computers at the end of the day is an office routine, and it does not involve people reviewing or controlling what an AI decides.
ww.Hiding AI outputs from people so that th: Hiding AI outputs from people prevents any review, so it removes oversight and does the opposite of what human oversight is meant to do.
ww.Letting the AI run with no review by peo: Letting the AI run with no review by people removes oversight altogether, and errors or bias could go uncaught, so this is the absence of human oversight.

rw: Denying medical treatment can seriously harm a person, so a human should review the decision and be able to override it instead of leaving it fully automated.

ww.Sorting incoming emails into folders: Sorting incoming emails into folders is a low-stakes task where a mistake is easy to fix, so full automation is acceptable and review is not essential.
ww.Spell checking a long draft report: Spell checking a draft is low-risk, and a wrong suggestion is easy to spot and undo, so it does not need to be kept under human review.
ww.Resizing images for a website page: Resizing images for a web page is routine and low-risk, with errors easy to see and fix, so it does not need human review.

rw: Surveillance concern with AI is about tracking people's activities, for example with face recognition, in ways that can invade their privacy and limit their freedom.

ww.Making videos higher resolution so camer: Making videos higher resolution is an improvement in image quality, and it does not by itself describe the privacy worry of tracking what people do.
ww.Making screens brighter so that they are: Brighter screens help people see content more easily, which is a display feature and has no link to the tracking of people.
ww.Making cameras cheaper to buy for homes: Cheaper cameras for homes and shops are a cost matter, and they are not the concern, which is the tracking of people by AI.

rw: Using face recognition on shoppers without telling them may invade their privacy without consent, which is the main concern raised by this scenario.

ww.It makes the whole store much quieter: Face recognition does not make a store quieter, and noise level has no link to the concern, which is about people being identified without being told.
ww.It guarantees better service for all: Nothing guarantees better service from face recognition, and even if it helped, doing it without telling shoppers still raises privacy and consent problems.
ww.It lowers the price of goods for all: Nothing here suggests lower prices, and cheaper goods would not remove the concern that shoppers are being identified without their knowledge or consent.

rw: Data ownership is about who has rights to control and use a set of data, including who may share it, sell it or change it.

ww.Who pays for the internet at the main of: Who pays for the internet at the office is a billing question and does not say who has rights to control and use a set of data.
ww.Who stores the data on a shelf or in a c: Who stores data on a shelf or in a cabinet only describes where it is kept, and holding data does not mean having the rights to control it.
ww.Who deletes the data first in the firm e: Who deletes the data first each year is a task assignment, and ownership is about rights and control over the data, not who performs deletion.

rw: A privacy policy is a statement explaining how an organization collects, uses and protects data, so people can understand what happens to their information.

ww.A chart of server speed over time that s: A chart of server speed over time is a performance report that shows how fast pages load, and it does not explain how data is handled.
ww.A password for a website that lets users: A password lets users sign in to an account, which is an access tool, and it does not describe how an organization treats personal data.
ww.A rule that blocks websites that do not: A privacy policy does not block websites that refuse terms, since it is a notice from an organization about its data practices, not a blocking rule.

rw: Before signing up, a user should check what data is collected and how it is shared, since this shows the privacy risks they are accepting.

ww.Only the color of the app icon on screen: The color of an app icon has no bearing on how your data is handled, so checking only that leaves your privacy risks unexamined.
ww.Nothing, since all apps are identical in: Apps differ in what data they collect and share, so saying they are all identical is false, and checking nothing leaves a user unaware of risks.
ww.Only how many ads appear on the screen: The number of ads on the screen is a matter of annoyance, and checking only that ignores what data is collected and shared, which affects privacy.

rw: Phishing is a scam that tricks people into giving away sensitive information, such as passwords or card numbers, often with fake emails or sites that look real.

ww.A hobby of catching fish in a lake or a: Catching fish with a rod is a hobby spelled similarly, but phishing in computing is a scam and not an outdoor activity.
ww.A method of encrypting files so that onl: Encrypting files so only the owner can read them is a protection method, while phishing is an attack that tries to trick people.
ww.A kind of data chart used to show shares: A chart showing shares of a total as slices is a pie chart, which is a data display, and it has no link to phishing scams.

rw: Not clicking and reporting the email is right, because an unexpected request for a password on a strange link is typical of phishing, and reporting helps protect others.

ww.Reply with your password now: Replying with your password gives it directly to a possible attacker, and real IT staff do not ask for passwords by email, so this is unsafe.
ww.Click and enter your password now: Clicking and entering your password on a strange link sends it to a possible scam site, which gives attackers access to your account.
ww.Forward it to all coworkers: Forwarding the email to all coworkers spreads the phishing message and puts more people at risk, so it should be reported through proper channels instead.

rw: Fairness in AI means systems should treat people equitably and avoid discrimination, so decisions do not disadvantage people because of traits such as race or gender.

ww.Systems should always be the cheapest to: Cheapest to run is a cost goal, not fairness, because fairness concerns how a system treats people and not how low its running cost is.
ww.Systems should hide how they work from e: Hiding how a system works from users and auditors goes against transparency and makes it hard to check for unfair treatment, so it is not fairness.
ww.Systems should favor large companies ove: Favoring large companies over small ones is unequal treatment, which goes against fairness, since fair systems do not give one group an unearned advantage.
